title: Encode the Readiness Gate
subtitle: Ready only when ALL four tasks are done
scenario: It is SD-1, 4:00 PM. The tracker shows all four tasks done. Encode the gate that decides readiness: the hire is Day-One Ready only when every task is done - not most, all. Route a clean hire to the package; anything blocked would go to escalation.
input: Task tracker for hire H-4021: accounts done, hardware done, access done, payroll done. No task is blocked. Gate rule: ready is true only when ALL four tasks are done AND none is blocked. Ready -> route to day-one-package; not ready -> route to escalation-path.
instructions: Read all four task states from the tracker.
Set allTasksDone and anyBlocked from the fan-in (all done, none blocked).
Set ready to true only when every task is done and none is blocked.
Route a ready hire to day-one-package, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Encode a readiness gate as JSON: allTasksDone, anyBlocked, ready (booleans), and route. Ready is true only when all four tasks are done and none is blocked; a ready hire routes to day-one-package.
successMessage: Gate encoded. Because every task is done, the hire is Day-One Ready and routes to the package.
editorHelper: Ready means ALL done - the fan-in is on every task, not most.

intro.heading: Before the package: fan in on all

sections.title: A gate is a join, not a sum
sections.body: The four branches ran in parallel; the gate is where they fan back in. Readiness is not 'most done' or a score - it is an AND across every task. One unfinished task means not ready.

sections.title: The orchestration invariant
sections.body: This is the concept the whole module exists to teach: one blocked task blocks the hire no matter how many others succeeded. That is what makes parallel work reliable instead of hopeful.

sections.title: Two clean exits
sections.body: The gate has exactly two routes: ready hires go to the package, everything else goes to escalation. No silent third path where a half-ready hire slips through.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A gate result the package and escalation both read. Because this run is clean, it routes to day-one-package; the medium tier blocks a task to send it the other way.

takeaway.heading: Gate encoded
